headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via ChatGPT Desktop’s file/screen/clipboard surfaces; Dagster adds no direct shared channel or write conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app file content, so malicious content could be interpreted as instructions. Dagster has no direct input channel or shared filesystem, so the pairwise pathway is indirect rather than default. Uncertainty about any external bridge escalates above low.
conditions: IF the operator copies Dagster-generated text into ChatGPT Desktop
IF ChatGPT Desktop ingests screenshots or files containing attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for this workflow
Use a strict prompt template that strips instructions from pasted content
Review any file or screenshot before sending it to ChatGPT Desktop
Separate Dagster artifacts from ChatGPT Desktop inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while Dagster exposes no file or network surfaces in the profile. That makes leakage plausible if sensitive Dagster artifacts are manually transferred into ChatGPT Desktop, but the pair itself does not show an automatic shared workspace. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are manually uploaded or screenshotted into ChatGPT Desktop
IF the transferred material contains secrets, PHI, or regulated data
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive Dagster artifacts to ChatGPT Desktop
Redact identifiers before upload
Use synthetic samples for debugging
Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell, and Dagster is profiled with no filesystem write, shell, or network egress. With no overlapping mutable write surface, a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant shared write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator adds locking-free mutable state
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared workflows
Do not mount a common writable directory
Add file locks if shared state is introduced
requires-engineering: introduce a coordinator for mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate code or analysis from files and screenshots, and Dagster is a data-orchestration system that could consume those outputs in a pipeline. The profiles do not prove Dagster automatically trusts ChatGPT Desktop, so this is an inferred handoff risk rather than a documented default. Uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF Dagster uses ChatGPT Desktop output as pipeline configuration or code without review
IF generated text is promoted into an automated Dagster asset or job definition
mitigations: Require human review before Dagster ingestion
Validate generated configs against schema
Run ChatGPT output in a staging pipeline first
Log provenance for any AI-generated artifact
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Dagster in the profile, while ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files and screenshots under OpenAI’s vendor-managed service. Because only one side has documented data handling details, the compliance risk is limited and mostly depends on what data the operator sends.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent from Dagster workflows into ChatGPT Desktop
IF the operator requires a residency or retention guarantee not documented for the pair
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ChatGPT Desktop
Use de-identified samples
Check vendor terms before sharing data
Document retention expectations for operators
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance review
